name: भक्तियोग
teaching: Between the formless absolute and the beloved with a face, Krishna gently favours the face — not because the formless is false, but because the embodied heart needs somewhere to rest. And if love is hard, practice; if practice is hard, work as offering; if even that is hard, simply let go of results. The chapter ends not with metaphysics but with a portrait of the devotee: friendly, compassionate, free of malice, the same in honour and disgrace. Between the formless and the beloved face, the Gita gently chooses the face — for embodied hearts love best what they can hold. A ladder is lowered to every capacity, and the chapter ends in the portrait the Lord calls dearest.
questions: Which rung of Krishna's ladder — absorption, practice, offered work, surrendered results — is actually within your reach this week?
Of the devotee's qualities listed at the end, which one is hardest for you?
Whom do you find easy to love — and is your spiritual life connected to that ease, or separate from it?

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.devanagari:
एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते ।
ये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः॥
verses.transliteration:
evaṃ satatayuktā ye bhaktāstvāṃ paryupāsate
ye cāpyakṣaramavyaktaṃ teṣāṃ ke yogavittamāḥ
verses.essence: Arjuna asks: the devotees who worship you thus, ever-disciplined — and those who worship the Imperishable, the Unmanifest — which of these knows yoga better?
verses.translation: Those devotees who, ever steadfast, thus worship Thee and those also who worship the imperishable and the unmanifested which of them are better versed in Yoga?

anvaya.parts: सतत (constant) + युक्त (yoked, devoted): constantly devoted

anvaya.base: परि + उप + √आस् · to worship all around, honour

anvaya.form: adjective used as noun, neuter, accusative singular (object)

anvaya.parts: योग (yoga) + वित् (knower, from √विद्) + तम (most): the best among those who know yoga

verses.explanation: The question the vision made urgent: should one love the Person just seen, or contemplate the formless Absolute behind him? Arjuna asks like an engineer — which path is *better* — and his 'evam', 'thus', points back to 11.55's portrait. The whole chapter is the answer to this one fork.
verses.connection: Born directly of ch11: form and formless both revealed — now which to worship?
verses.reflection: Hold your own version of the fork honestly today: does your heart pray to a face, or a vastness?
verses.background: Arjuna, having seen both the cosmic blaze and the beloved face, asks the question the vision forced: of those who worship You with steadfast love, and those who seek the imperishable unmanifest — which are the better knowers of yoga?
verses.hook: Who is the better yogi: one who loves God's form or seeks the formless?

views.text: Takes 'thus' as pointing back to 11.55. The second group are renunciates meditating on the Immutable, called unmanifest because it is free of all limiting adjuncts and beyond the reach of the senses.
Reads the Imperishable and Unmanifest here as the individual self in its true nature, not the supreme Brahman, and hears the question as: which of the two groups reaches its goal sooner?
Earlier chapters praised both the devotee and the man of knowledge as the best, so Arjuna asks which is finally better: worship of the Lord with attributes or contemplation of the attributeless.
Arjuna's question presumes God has both a formless aspect and a personal form; limiting God to either one is a mistake, though the path of worshipping the formless is said to be very hard.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.devanagari:
मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ।
श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः॥
verses.transliteration:
mayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate
śraddhayā parayopetāste me yuktatamā matāḥ
verses.essence: The Blessed Lord says: those who, fixing their mind on me, worship me ever-disciplined and endowed with supreme faith — them I hold to be the most yoked.
verses.translation: Those who, fixing their mind on Me, worship Me, ever steadfast and endowed with supreme faith, are the best in Yoga in My opinion.

anvaya.form: gerund of the causative (having made enter)

anvaya.parts: नित्य (always) + युक्त (yoked, devoted): always devoted

anvaya.form: adjective, feminine, instrumental singular (with), agreeing with श्रद्धया

anvaya.base: उप + √इ · to approach, be possessed of

anvaya.form: pronoun, genitive singular, short form (by me, with मताः)

anvaya.parts: युक्त (yoked) + तम (most): the most yoked

anvaya.form: past passive participle, masculine, nominative plural (considered)

verses.explanation: A direct answer, rare in scripture: the form-lovers win — yuktatamāḥ, the same superlative that crowned 6.47. The deciding factors are named: āveśya, the mind not merely directed at him but *immersed*; and śraddhā parā, the highest grade of trust. Concreteness, it turns out, is not a concession but an advantage: love needs a face to find its full strength.
verses.connection: Answers 12.1 cleanly — then immediately honors the other path in 12.3–4.
verses.reflection: Let love have a face today — fix the mind on the concrete sacred and feel devotion gain traction.
verses.background: Krishna answers with a tenderness the tradition treasures: both reach Me, but those whose minds are fixed on Me with supreme faith I deem the most yoked — for the unmanifest path is steep for embodied beings, while those who offer all to Me and meditate on Me with undivided yoga, I swiftly lift from the ocean of death and rebirth.
verses.hook: Whom does Krishna count as the most perfect in yoga?

refs.note: The one God lies hidden in all beings, pervading everything as the inner Self of all.
The knowers of truth say the one Reality is called Brahman, Paramātmā and Bhagavān; this frames the personal form as God's closest realization.

views.text: The form meant is the Cosmic form of 11. They are rightly called the best yogis because their minds stay fixed on him day and night; the verdict on the other group is held back for the next verses.
Stresses that these worshippers hold him as exceedingly dear and long for constant union; worshipping him as their supreme goal, they reach him soon and easily.
Fixing the mind on the Lord is here a spontaneous, unforced becoming-one with him, and the verse is a solemn declaration by the Lord.

God is realized at different distances, as formless Brahman, as the Supreme Soul within, and as the personal Lord; devotees who worship the personal form with faith know him most closely and are the highest yogis.

verses.devanagari:
ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते ।
सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यञ्च कूटस्थमचलन्ध्रुवम्॥
verses.transliteration:
ye tvakṣaramanirdeśyamavyaktaṃ paryupāsate
sarvatragamacintyañca kūṭasthamacalandhruvam
verses.essence: But those who worship the Imperishable — the undefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, summit-still, immovable, constant —
verses.translation: Those who worship the imperishable, the indefinable, the unmanifest, the omnipresent, the unthinkable, the immovable, and the eternal.

anvaya.form: adjective used as noun, neuter, accusative singular (object)

anvaya.base: अ + निर् + √दिश् · not to be pointed out
anvaya.form: gerundive, neuter, accusative singular (that cannot be defined)

anvaya.base: परि + उप + √आस् · to worship all around, honour

anvaya.parts: सर्वत्र (everywhere) + ग (going): that which goes everywhere

anvaya.form: gerundive, neuter, accusative singular (that cannot be conceived)

anvaya.base: कूटस्थ · standing like an anvil, changeless
anvaya.parts: कूट (anvil, peak) + स्थ (standing): standing fixed like an anvil

verses.explanation: The other path described in its own austere vocabulary — eight epithets in two lines, most of them negations or abstractions, each word a door closing on imagery: undefinable, unmanifest, unthinkable. To worship *this* is to hold the mind to what gives the mind nothing to hold. The sentence itself withholds its main clause until the next verse — even the grammar makes you wait.
verses.connection: Begins the honest account of the formless path before its difficulty is weighed in 12.5.
verses.reflection: Spend two minutes with the attributeless — no image, no name — and honor those who dwell there.
verses.background: Krishna answers with a tenderness the tradition treasures: both reach Me, but those whose minds are fixed on Me with supreme faith I deem the most yoked — for the unmanifest path is steep for embodied beings, while those who offer all to Me and meditate on Me with undivided yoga, I swiftly lift from the ocean of death and rebirth.
verses.text_note: The translation of this verse was missing in the source dataset; it is taken from the Sivananda text in the gita/gita dataset.
verses.hook: What about those who worship the formless, unthinkable Imperishable?

views.text: Reads every epithet as the individual self: indefinable because it is other than the body, all-pervading because it dwells in all bodies yet cannot be thought of in their terms, immovable because it never leaves its own nature.
Those who contemplate the motionless Self still superimpose on it the Lord's attributes, which is what epithets like 'all-pervading' express.
Krishna does not reject worship of the formless: those devoted to the unmanifest, all-pervading Brahman also reach him, and no one should claim their own idea of God is the only true one.

verses.devanagari:
सन्नियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः ।
ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः॥
verses.transliteration:
sanniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ sarvatra samabuddhayaḥ
te prāpnuvanti māmeva sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ
verses.essence: — restraining the host of senses, even-minded everywhere, delighting in the welfare of all beings: they also reach none but me.
verses.translation: Having restrained all the senses, even-minded everywhere, intent on the welfare of all beings verily they also come unto Me.

anvaya.base: सम् + नि + √यम् · to hold in, restrain

anvaya.parts: इन्द्रिय (sense) + ग्राम (group, village): the whole set of senses
सम (even) + बुद्धि (understanding): those whose understanding is even

anvaya.meaning: in the welfare of all beings
anvaya.parts: सर्व (all) + भूत (beings) + हित (welfare): the welfare of all beings

verses.explanation: The formless path completed, with its signature ethics: total sense-governance, evenness everywhere, and — the warmth inside the austerity — sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ, joy in every creature's good. And the destination clause settles all rivalry: mām eva, *me alone*. There were never two summits; the impersonal seekers arrive at the same person by another face.
verses.connection: Closes the question of destination — both roads end in him — leaving only the question of cost.
verses.reflection: Whichever path you walk, keep its ethic today: senses governed, delight in every being's welfare.
verses.background: Krishna answers with a tenderness the tradition treasures: both reach Me, but those whose minds are fixed on Me with supreme faith I deem the most yoked — for the unmanifest path is steep for embodied beings, while those who offer all to Me and meditate on Me with undivided yoga, I swiftly lift from the ocean of death and rebirth.
verses.hook: Do seekers of the formless also reach God in the end?

views.text: It goes without saying that they reach him: the man of knowledge is the Lord's very Self (7.18), so it is out of place to ask whether such people are the best among yogis.
Their evenness comes from seeing every self, in any body, as alike a knower. 'Reach me' means they realise a self that, in its freedom from samsara, is like his.
Once likes and dislikes are destroyed through meditation on the Self, the yogi turns to the welfare of others, serves without tiring, and gives fearlessness to every creature.
Those who worship the formless with restrained senses, even minds and care for all beings also attain him, since God meets each seeker in the aspect they choose, here as the all-pervading Brahman.

verses.devanagari:
क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम् ।
अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते॥
verses.transliteration:
kleśo'dhikatarasteṣāmavyaktāsaktacetasām
avyaktā hi gatirduḥkhaṃ dehavadbhiravāpyate
verses.essence: Greater is the toil of those whose minds are set on the Unmanifest, for the unmanifest goal is reached by the embodied only with difficulty.
verses.translation: Greater is their trouble whose minds are set on the unmanifested; for the goal; the unmanifested, is very hard for the embodied to reach.

anvaya.meaning: whose minds are set on the Unmanifest
anvaya.base: अव्यक्तासक्तचेतस् · mind attached to the unmanifest
anvaya.parts: अव्यक्त (unmanifest) + आसक्त (attached) + चेतस् (mind): those whose mind is attached to the unmanifest

anvaya.form: adjective, feminine, nominative singular, agreeing with गतिः
noun, neuter, accusative singular used as adverb (painfully)
adjective used as noun, masculine, instrumental plural (by)
verb, present passive, 3rd person singular (is reached)

verses.explanation: The cost accounting: kleśo 'dhikataraḥ — more friction, not less truth. The reason is in one word: dehavadbhiḥ, *by those who have bodies*. Embodied beings love through eyes, hands, voice; asking such creatures to adore a featureless absolute is asking a river to flow without banks. The formless path is honored — and priced for what it asks of incarnate hearts.
verses.connection: The practical verdict behind 12.2's ranking: same summit, steeper face.
verses.reflection: Be kind to your embodiment today — you love through eyes and hands; let your practice use them.
verses.background: Krishna answers with a tenderness the tradition treasures: both reach Me, but those whose minds are fixed on Me with supreme faith I deem the most yoked — for the unmanifest path is steep for embodied beings, while those who offer all to Me and meditate on Me with undivided yoga, I swiftly lift from the ocean of death and rebirth.
verses.hook: Why is the path to the formless so much harder for us?

views.text: The difficulty is that one must give up identifying with the body; 'the embodied' means those who take the body to be themselves.

These seekers take on a double labour: they first superimpose the divine attributes on the Self and then contemplate it, while the Lord, already possessed of those attributes, is available without effort.

Fixing the restless mind on the attributeless demands a sharp, subtle, one-pointed intellect, the fourfold qualification, and hearing, reflection and meditation under a teacher established in Brahman.

We are embodied beings used to forms, so the mind finds no hold on the formless; and the attributeless Brahman offers no grace, so its seekers must cling by their own effort like a baby monkey, while devotees are carried like kittens.

verses.devanagari:
ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः ।
अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते॥
verses.transliteration:
ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparāḥ
ananyenaiva yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate
verses.essence: But those who, renouncing all actions in me and holding me supreme, worship me, meditating with a yoga turned to no other —
verses.translation: But to those who worship Me, renouncing all actions in Me, regarding Me as the supreme gaol, meditating on Me with single-minded Yoga.

anvaya.base: सम् + नि + √अस् · to lay down, renounce

anvaya.parts: मत् (me) + पर (highest): those for whom I am the highest

anvaya.form: present participle, masculine, nominative plural (while meditating)

verses.explanation: The recommended path drawn in full: every action deposited in him (the trustee-relation of 3.30 returning), him as the one direction, meditation that does not glance sideways. Ananyena — a key word across the Gita (8.14, 9.22, 13.10) — no second object, no hedge, no backup deity. The sentence leans forward into the promise of the next verse.
verses.connection: Describes the devotee whose rescue 12.7 will announce.
verses.reflection: Deposit every action in Him today as you act — sannyasya mayi — and meditate on no second thing.
verses.background: Krishna answers with a tenderness the tradition treasures: both reach Me, but those whose minds are fixed on Me with supreme faith I deem the most yoked — for the unmanifest path is steep for embodied beings, while those who offer all to Me and meditate on Me with undivided yoga, I swiftly lift from the ocean of death and rebirth.
verses.hook: What do those who give all their actions to God do?

views.text: These devotees dedicate all actions to God, accept him as supreme and meditate on him with single-minded yoga, meaning a yoga with no object other than the Cosmic Deity, the Self.
'All actions' includes eating and other acts that sustain the body as well as Vedic rites; and the worship itself — meditation, praise, prostration — is so dear to them that it is its own end.
Ananya means a yoga in which there is no other to be worshipped; for such single-minded devotees success comes without strain, by the Lord's grace.
Even on the path of devotion one does not abandon action: one keeps acting and offers the fruits to the Lord.
Devotees of the personal form easily engage mind and senses in God through his names, form and pastimes, and so quickly unite their consciousness with him.

verses.devanagari:
तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् ।
भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम्॥
verses.transliteration:
teṣāmahaṃ samuddhartā mṛtyusaṃsārasāgarāt
bhavāmi nacirātpārtha mayyāveśitacetasām
verses.essence: — for them I become, before long, the deliverer from the ocean of death-bound existence, Partha, their minds absorbed in me.
verses.translation: To those whose minds are set on Me, O Arjuna, verily I become ere long the saviour out of the ocean of Samsara.

anvaya.base: सम् + उद् + √हृ · to lift up and out
anvaya.form: agent noun, masculine, nominative singular (one who lifts out)

anvaya.meaning: from the ocean of death-bound worldly life
anvaya.parts: मृत्यु (death) + संसार (cycle of births) + सागर (ocean): the ocean that is samsara bound up with death
न (not) + चिरात् (after a long time): not after long
आवेशित (made to enter) + चेतस् (mind): those whose mind has been made to enter

verses.explanation: The chapter's central transaction, and the grammar carries the theology: ahaṁ samuddhartā — *I* am the lifter-out. On the formless path the seeker swims the ocean; on this one, the Ocean's master reaches down. Na cirāt, without delay: grace does not keep office hours. The devotee's one task was completed in the previous verse — being findable, mind already in him.
verses.connection: The payoff of 12.6's surrender — and the deepest reason 12.2 ranked this path first.
verses.reflection: When the ocean feels wide today, remember who lifts the surrendered — and stop swimming alone.
verses.background: Krishna answers with a tenderness the tradition treasures: both reach Me, but those whose minds are fixed on Me with supreme faith I deem the most yoked — for the unmanifest path is steep for embodied beings, while those who offer all to Me and meditate on Me with undivided yoga, I swiftly lift from the ocean of death and rebirth.
verses.hook: How quickly does God rescue those whose minds rest in him?

views.text: Samsara is fraught with death and is called a sea because it is so hard to cross; the 'I' who lifts them out is the Cosmic Person on whom their minds are fixed.
Samsara is called deadly because it stands in the way of reaching him; to those who worship only for its own sake he becomes the saviour soon.
The one lifted is the devotee whose surrender is total and ungrudging, who leaves himself at the Lord's mercy and has given up even the idea of liberation.
Because devotees offer their hearts without break, God soon gives his grace, removes their obstacles and himself becomes their savior from the cycle of birth and death.

verses.devanagari:
मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय ।
निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः॥
verses.transliteration:
mayyeva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya
nivasiṣyasi mayyeva ata ūrdhvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
verses.essence: Place your mind in me alone; let your understanding enter into me. You will dwell in me thereafter — of this there is no doubt.
verses.translation: Fix thy mind in Me only, thy intellect in Me, (then) thou shalt no doubt live in Me alone hereafter.

anvaya.form: imperative, 2nd person singular, middle voice (a command)

verses.explanation: The instruction at its purest, the ladder's top rung stated first: both faculties — manas, the feeling, flowing mind, and buddhi, the deciding intellect — given one address, mayy eva, in me alone. The promise uses the language of residence: nivasiṣyasi, you will *live* in me, not visit; Śaṅkara takes 'hereafter' as after the body falls. And the chapter's gentlest reassurance closes it: na saṁśayaḥ, no doubt — spoken to the man whose doubts have filled eleven chapters.
verses.connection: Step one of the famous ladder (12.8–11): the ideal, stated first so the descents have a summit.
verses.reflection: Try the ideal first, tonight: mind placed in Him, intellect entered into Him — and dwell, doubtless.
verses.background: A ladder is lowered rung by rung to every capacity: fix mind and intellect in Me and dwell in Me — if you cannot, reach Me by repeated practice; if not that, work for My sake; if even that is beyond you, then do your duty and renounce the fruit — for the renunciation of fruit brings immediate peace.
verses.hook: Where should you place your mind and intellect to live in God?

refs.note: The mind decides bondage and freedom: attached to the world it binds, turned to God it liberates; hence the call to fix the mind on God.
Bondage and liberation are decided by the state of the mind.
Akrūra names the intellect's errors: taking the self for the body, the passing for lasting, and pain for pleasure; this is why it must be surrendered to God.

views.text: Manas is the power of thinking and doubting, buddhi the power that decides; 'hereafter' means after the body falls, and 'dwell in me' means living in identity with him.
Reads 'hereafter' as immediately: as soon as the mind is fixed with the conviction that he alone is the goal, one already lives in him.
Concentration forced by posture and effort still keeps the sense of meditator and meditated; the real awakening rises by itself, without fuel, and only then is the Lord realised.
Krishna asks for two things: absorb the mind in God, since God counts mental rather than merely physical acts, and surrender the intellect to him, as we follow a doctor beyond our own knowledge.

verses.devanagari:
अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् ।
अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय॥
verses.transliteration:
atha cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram
abhyāsayogena tato māmicchāptuṃ dhanañjaya
verses.essence: But if you cannot fix your mind steadily on me, then seek to reach me by the yoga of repeated practice, Dhananjaya.
verses.translation: If thou art unable to fix thy mind steadily on Me, then by the Yoga of constant practice do thou seek to reach Me, O Arjuna.

anvaya.base: सम् + आ + √धा · to put together, concentrate

anvaya.form: adjective, neuter, accusative singular used as adverb (steadily)

anvaya.parts: अभ्यास (repeated practice) + योग (discipline): the discipline that consists in repetition
धनम् (wealth) + जय (winning): one who wins wealth

verses.explanation: The first 'if you cannot' — three words that make this chapter the kindest in the Gita. Steady absorption unavailable? Then abhyāsa: the unsteady version, done again and again, the mind brought back each time it strays (6.26's old patience). The ladder's genius is that no rung shames the one below it; each is simply where someone real is standing.
verses.connection: Rung two: when 12.8's steadiness is out of reach, repetition is the road to it.
verses.reflection: Cannot hold steady? Then repeat: return the mind each time it strays — abhyasa is the unsteady's road.
verses.background: A ladder is lowered rung by rung to every capacity: fix mind and intellect in Me and dwell in Me — if you cannot, reach Me by repeated practice; if not that, work for My sake; if even that is beyond you, then do your duty and renounce the fruit — for the renunciation of fruit brings immediate peace.
verses.hook: What if you cannot keep your mind steady on God yet?

views.text: Practice means repeatedly drawing the mind back from everything else and fixing it on a single object; the concentration that results is the yoga of practice.
The repetition is loving remembrance: dwelling again and again on his boundless qualities — beauty, compassion, sweetness, majesty, omniscience — until the mind settles on him.
The mind's entry into the Lord is hard without a strong descent of grace and long service to one's teachers, so practice is prescribed.
The name Dhananjaya is a hint: one who won great wealth for Yudhishthira's sacrifice can conquer the mind and win the wealth of Self-knowledge.
Those who cannot yet fix the mind on God should practise remembrance, bringing the wandering mind back to his names, forms and qualities again and again.

verses.devanagari:
अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव ।
मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन्सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि॥
verses.transliteration:
abhyāse'pyasamartho'si matkarmaparamo bhava
madarthamapi karmāṇi kurvansiddhimavāpsyasi
verses.essence: If you are incapable even of practice, be intent on working for me; even doing actions for my sake, you will attain perfection.
verses.translation: If thou art unable to practise even this Abhyasa Yoga, be thou intent on doing actions for My sake; even by doing actions for My sake, thou shalt attain perfection.

anvaya.parts: मत् (me) + कर्म (work) + परम (highest): one for whom work for me is highest
मत् (me) + अर्थम् (for the sake of): for my sake

anvaya.form: present participle, masculine, nominative singular (while doing)

verses.explanation: Rung three descends from the mind to the hands: cannot sit and practice? Then *do* — but do for him. Mad-artham, for my sake: the same workday, re-addressed, becomes worship; cooking, building, fighting, healing — each act a letter posted to one recipient. Perfection, the verse insists, is reachable through the calendar as surely as through the cushion.
verses.connection: Rung three: contemplation replaced by consecrated action — the karma-yoga of Part One, now love-shaped.
verses.reflection: Cannot even practice? Re-address one task today: done for His sake — and let work become the worship.
verses.background: A ladder is lowered rung by rung to every capacity: fix mind and intellect in Me and dwell in Me — if you cannot, reach Me by repeated practice; if not that, work for My sake; if even that is beyond you, then do your duty and renounce the fruit — for the renunciation of fruit brings immediate peace.
verses.hook: If steady practice is too hard, what simpler way is offered?

views.text: Works done for him lead to perfection gradually: first purity of mind, then concentration, then knowledge.
'My works' are devotional acts: building temples, laying out gardens, lighting lamps, sweeping shrines, gathering flowers, chanting his names. Done with love, they steady the mind as practice would.
Takes 'works for me' as acts done to please him, such as Ekādaśī fasting, vows and singing his names; doing these alone, one gains liberation.
Those who cannot remember God constantly can keep doing their usual work but change the intention, doing it all for God's pleasure; this steadies the mind and slowly grows love for him.

verses.devanagari:
अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः ।
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान्॥
verses.transliteration:
athaitadapyaśakto'si kartuṃ madyogamāśritaḥ
sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ tataḥ kuru yatātmavān
verses.essence: If you cannot do even this, then, taking refuge in my yoga, renounce the fruit of all action with the self subdued.
verses.translation: If thou art unable to do even this, then, resorting to union with Me, renounce the fruits of all actions with the self controlled.

anvaya.parts: मत् (me) + योग (discipline): the discipline that rests on me

anvaya.form: past participle, masculine, nominative singular (having resorted to)

anvaya.meaning: renouncing the fruit of all actions
anvaya.base: सर्वकर्मफलत्याग · giving up all works' fruits
anvaya.parts: सर्व (all) + कर्म (action) + फल (fruit) + त्याग (giving up): giving up the fruit of all actions
यत (restrained) + आत्मन् (self, mind) + वत् (having): one possessed of a restrained self

verses.explanation: The lowest rung, and the most widely reachable: cannot even dedicate the work? Then keep working as you do — only let go of the outcome, with the self held in check. One thread of devotion stays: mad-yogam āśritaḥ, taking refuge in him, and the commentators read the release as handing the results over to him. No altered schedule; just the open hand where the clutch used to be. The ladder bottoms out at something anyone can begin this afternoon. No one is left without a first step.
verses.connection: The final concession — which 12.12 will reveal is no concession at all.
verses.reflection: Cannot manage even that? Then do today's duties and release the results — the lowest rung lifts too.
verses.background: A ladder is lowered rung by rung to every capacity: fix mind and intellect in Me and dwell in Me — if you cannot, reach Me by repeated practice; if not that, work for My sake; if even that is beyond you, then do your duty and renounce the fruit — for the renunciation of fruit brings immediate peace.
verses.hook: If you cannot even work for God, what is left to do?

views.text: If unable even to work intent on the Lord, Arjuna should resort to Yoga for him, doing works dedicated to him, and then, with mind controlled, give up the results of all works.

If even works for him are beyond you, turn to contemplating the self taught in the first six chapters, with renunciation of fruit as its means; once body-identification falls away, devotion to the Lord arises by itself.
If you do not know the methods the scriptures lay down, simply offer yourself to him; he cites his own prayer asking the Lord to forgive every flawed act.
Do your duties as the Lord commands, as far as you can, and leave their results, seen or unseen, in his hands; laying the burden on him, you will be fulfilled by his grace.
For those not yet convinced of their bond with God, the fourth option is to keep working but let go of the fruits; this detachment purifies the mind and readies the intellect for higher practice.

verses.devanagari:
श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते ।
ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम्॥
verses.transliteration:
śreyo hi jñānamabhyāsājjñānāddhyānaṃ viśiṣyate
dhyānātkarmaphalatyāgastyāgācchāntiranantaram
verses.essence: Better than practice is knowledge; better than knowledge, meditation; better than meditation, the renunciation of action's fruit — from renunciation, peace immediately.
verses.translation: Better indeed is knowledge than practice; than knowledge meditation is better; than meditation the renunciation of the fruits of actions: peace immediately follows renunciation.

anvaya.parts: कर्म (action) + फल (fruit) + त्याग (giving up): giving up the fruit of action

verses.explanation: The chapter's sly reversal: the rung offered last as a concession is here ranked *first*. Knowledge above practice, meditation above knowledge, and above meditation the renunciation of fruit, with peace immediately after. The ranking puzzles on first reading; Śaṅkara treats it as praise meant to rouse interest in the humblest discipline. Read practically, the point holds: rote practice, book-knowledge, even meditation can all be performed by an ego still gripping its outcomes, while phala-tyāga is the grip itself released. And the timing claim is bold: śāntir anantaram — peace not after lifetimes, but immediately. The hand opens; the war ends.
verses.connection: Re-values the ladder of 12.8–11: the humblest rung touches the goal most directly — and opens the portrait that follows.
verses.reflection: Take the shortcut hidden at the bottom today: renounce one outcome and collect the immediate peace.
verses.background: A ladder is lowered rung by rung to every capacity: fix mind and intellect in Me and dwell in Me — if you cannot, reach Me by repeated practice; if not that, work for My sake; if even that is beyond you, then do your duty and renounce the fruit — for the renunciation of fruit brings immediate peace.
verses.hook: Why does letting go of results bring peace faster than knowledge or meditation?

views.text: The ranking is praise, meant to rouse interest: as present-day Brahmins are honoured by the story of Agastya drinking the sea, the unenlightened man's renunciation of fruit shares in the glory of the sage's renunciation of all desire.
Read as steps in reverse: works done without desire destroy sin and bring peace; peace makes meditation on the self possible; meditation gives self-realisation; and from that comes supreme devotion.

Reads a causal chain: knowledge, the mind's entry into the Lord, makes absorption possible, and only then can one renounce fruits, for how could one renounce in what is unknown? So knowledge is the root.

The verse orders the stages: mechanical ritual is lower than spiritual knowledge, knowledge lower than meditation that controls the mind, and that leads to giving up the fruits of action, which brings peace.

verses.devanagari:
अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च ।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी॥
verses.transliteration:
adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca
nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ samaduḥkhasukhaḥ kṣamī
verses.essence: Without hatred toward any being, friendly and compassionate, free of 'mine' and free of 'I', equal in sorrow and joy, forbearing —
verses.translation: He who hates no creature, who is friendly and compassionate to all, who is free from attachment and egoism, balanced in pleasure and pain, and forgiving.

anvaya.parts: अ (not) + द्वेष्टृ (hater, from √द्विष्): one who does not hate
सर्व (all) + भूत (being): all beings
निर् (without) + मम (mine): one without the sense of 'mine'
निर् (without) + अहङ्कार (I-maker, ego): one without the sense of 'I'

anvaya.base: समदुःखसुख · same in sorrow and joy
anvaya.parts: सम (same) + दुःख (pain) + सुख (pleasure): one to whom pain and pleasure are the same

verses.explanation: The beloved-devotee portrait begins (12.13–19), one of the Gita's most cherished passages. First the foundation, and it is social before it is mystical: adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānām, hating no being — not even those who might seem to qualify. Then maitraḥ, karuṇaḥ: friendship and compassion as default settings. Then the two inner releases, nirmamaḥ and nirahaṅkāraḥ, free of 'mine' and of 'I', and the evenness and forbearance that follow from them. Notice what is absent from the whole portrait: no austerities, no visions, no learning. The saint is described entirely by how it feels to be near them.
verses.connection: Opens the answer to an unasked question: what does 12.12's released person actually look like?
verses.reflection: Run the foundation check today: hating no being, friendly, compassionate — begin the portrait there.
verses.background: The chapter closes with the portrait of the devotee dear to Krishna: hating none, friendly and compassionate, free of 'I' and 'mine', even in pleasure and pain, content, self-governed, agitating no one and unagitated, the same in honor and disgrace — and the seal: those who follow this immortal dharma with faith, holding Me supreme, are exceedingly dear to Me.
verses.hook: How does a devotee dear to God treat others and the self?

views.text: He hates nothing, not even what causes him sorrow, because he sees all beings as his own Self; compassionate, he grants safety to every creature, as a monk does.
He does not hate even those who wrong him, thinking the Lord moves them to it so that his own past faults are worked off; the portrait describes the karma-yogin who worships through his work.
Sorts the three by who is met: no hatred toward those above, friendship toward equals, compassion toward those below.
Verses 13 to 19 describe the devotees God loves: free of malice since all are parts of God, kind and compassionate, humble and free of pride, even in joy and sorrow, and quick to forgive.

verses.devanagari:
सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः ।
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः॥
verses.transliteration:
santuṣṭaḥ satataṃ yogī yatātmā dṛḍhaniścayaḥ
mayyarpitamanobuddhiryo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ
verses.essence: — ever content, a yogi, self-governed, of firm resolve, with mind and understanding offered to me: that devotee of mine is dear to me.
verses.translation: Ever content, steady in meditation, self-controlled, possessed of firm conviction, with the mind and intellect dedicated to Me, he, My devotee, is dear to Me.

anvaya.parts: यत (restrained) + आत्मन् (self): one whose self is restrained
दृढ (firm) + निश्चय (conviction): one whose conviction is firm

anvaya.base: अर्पितमनोबुद्धि · who has offered mind and intellect
anvaya.parts: अर्पित (offered) + मनस् (mind) + बुद्धि (intellect): one whose mind and intellect are offered
मद् (me) + भक्त (devotee): a devotee of me

anvaya.form: pronoun, genitive/dative singular, short form (to/for me)

verses.explanation: Santuṣṭaḥ satatam — content *always*, contentment uncoupled from supply. Dṛḍha-niścayaḥ: gentleness, the portrait insists, is not vagueness; the soft-hearted devotee has a spine of resolve. And then the refrain enters that will toll through the rest of the chapter: sa me priyaḥ — that one is dear to me. God confessing, repeatedly, whom he loves.
verses.connection: First sounding of the chapter's refrain — the divine 'dear to me' that structures 12.14–19.
verses.reflection: Be content once today with what is, while staying firm about what you are doing — both at once.
verses.background: The chapter closes with the portrait of the devotee dear to Krishna: hating none, friendly and compassionate, free of 'I' and 'mine', even in pleasure and pain, content, self-governed, agitating no one and unagitated, the same in honor and disgrace — and the seal: those who follow this immortal dharma with faith, holding Me supreme, are exceedingly dear to Me.
verses.hook: What inner qualities make a devotee dear to God?

views.text: This verse spells out what 7.17 hinted, that the man of knowledge is very dear to the Lord; his 'firm conviction' concerns the reality of the Self.
The yogi here ever contemplates the self as distinct from the body, and offers mind and reason in the conviction that Vāsudeva, pleased by selfless work, will grant the vision of the self.
He is a yogi at all times because his inner faculty stays completely quiet even while he is busy with worldly dealings.

These devotees are content because they want little, steadily absorbed in God, self-controlled, firm in conviction from scripture and the Guru, and have given mind and intellect to God, so the rest of life follows.

verses.devanagari:
यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः ।
हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः॥
verses.transliteration:
yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ
harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ
verses.essence: One from whom the world does not shrink, and who does not shrink from the world; freed from elation, impatience, fear and agitation — that one is dear to me.
verses.translation: He by whom the world is not agitated and who cannot be agitated by the world, and who is freed from joy, anger, fear and anxiety he is dear to Me.

anvaya.meaning: from elation, impatience, fear and anxiety
anvaya.form: noun, masculine, instrumental plural (from, with मुक्तः)
anvaya.parts: हर्ष (elation) + अमर्ष (impatience) + भय (fear) + उद्वेग (anxiety): a list of four, joined by 'and'

anvaya.form: pronoun, genitive/dative singular, short form (to/for me)

verses.explanation: A two-way peace treaty with existence: na udvijate, twice — the world is not disturbed by them, and they are not disturbed by the world. Such a person is, in the deepest sense, *safe* — safe to be around, safe inside themselves. Then harṣāmarṣa-bhayodvegair muktaḥ: free of four named turbulences — elation, impatience, fear and anxiety — the weather they no longer generate or import. It is the portrait's social test: the realized person shows up first as someone no creature needs to fear.
verses.connection: The portrait's social test: the devotee as a still point the world can rest near.
verses.reflection: Aim at the double peace today: agitate no one, and let no one's agitation move into you.
verses.background: The chapter closes with the portrait of the devotee dear to Krishna: hating none, friendly and compassionate, free of 'I' and 'mine', even in pleasure and pain, content, self-governed, agitating no one and unagitated, the same in honor and disgrace — and the seal: those who follow this immortal dharma with faith, holding Me supreme, are exceedingly dear to Me.
verses.hook: Who neither disturbs the world nor is disturbed by it?

refs.note: All divine virtues appear in those devoted to the Lord, while the undevoted, whatever methods they try, chase their own minds; it explains why these qualities grow in devotees.

views.text: Glosses the four: harṣa is elation at gaining something dear, showing as thrilled hair and tears; amarṣa is intolerance; bhaya is fright; udvega is distress.
He fears no one because he is certain he bears the world no enmity; so he neither favours some nor bristles at others.
Takes amarṣa as intolerance of another's gain, and udvega as the mind's agitation that fear and the rest produce.

Good qualities are the soul's natural state and shine once devotion cleans the mind; such devotees harm no one, stay gentle toward those who harm them, and are free of fear and anxiety because they are detached and accept God's will.

verses.devanagari:
अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः ।
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः॥
verses.transliteration:
anapekṣaḥ śucirdakṣa udāsīno gatavyathaḥ
sarvārambhaparityāgī yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ
verses.essence: Expecting nothing, pure, capable, impartial, untroubled, renouncing every self-serving undertaking — that devotee of mine is dear to me.
verses.translation: He who is free from wants, pure, expert, unconcerned, and free from pain, renouncing all undertakings or commencements he who is (thus) devoted to Me, is dear to Me.

anvaya.parts: अन् (without) + अपेक्षा (expectation): one without expectations
गत (gone) + व्यथा (distress): one whose distress has gone
सर्व (all) + आरम्भ (undertaking) + परित्यागिन् (one who gives up): one who gives up all undertakings
मद् (me) + भक्त (devotee): a devotee of me

anvaya.form: pronoun, genitive/dative singular, short form (to/for me)

verses.explanation: Note dakṣaḥ — *skillful*, expert: the beloved devotee is not vague or otherworldly but competent, sharp at their work; holiness here includes craftsmanship. Anapekṣaḥ, expecting nothing: the quiet engine of all the rest. Sarvārambha-parityāgī: not the end of activity, but of the scheming kind — projects launched to inflate a self.
verses.connection: Corrects the stereotype mid-portrait: detachment wedded to excellence.
verses.reflection: Pair purity with skill today — be the devotee who is also simply excellent at the work.
verses.background: The chapter closes with the portrait of the devotee dear to Krishna: hating none, friendly and compassionate, free of 'I' and 'mine', even in pleasure and pain, content, self-governed, agitating no one and unagitated, the same in honor and disgrace — and the seal: those who follow this immortal dharma with faith, holding Me supreme, are exceedingly dear to Me.
verses.hook: What kind of person, expecting nothing for themselves, is dear to God?

views.text: Dakṣa is one who grasps promptly and rightly the duty at hand; udāsīna is the monk who takes no side; the undertakings given up are works begun for results here or hereafter.
Reads each word against scripture: pure by eating what the śāstra allows, expert in the rites it prescribes, and giving up every undertaking it does not require.
His skill comes from having merged his will in the cosmic will: with no personal preference in the way, he acts swiftly and well.
Devotees rich in love for God are indifferent to worldly gain, pure inside and out, skilful because they treat work as service, carefree in his protection, and free of selfish motives.

verses.devanagari:
यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः॥
verses.transliteration:
yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati
śubhāśubhaparityāgī bhaktimānyaḥ sa me priyaḥ
verses.essence: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, who has given up both good and evil deeds — full of devotion, that one is dear to me.
verses.translation: He who neither rejoices, nor hates, nor grieves, nor desires, renouncing good and evil, and who is full of devotion, is dear to Me.

anvaya.meaning: who gives up good and evil
anvaya.base: शुभाशुभपरित्यागिन् · renouncer of good and bad
anvaya.parts: शुभ (good) + अशुभ (evil) + परित्यागिन् (one who gives up): one who gives up both good and evil deeds

anvaya.form: pronoun, genitive/dative singular, short form (to/for me)

verses.explanation: Four verbs of the heart's old weather — exulting, hating, mourning, wanting — all quieted; even the moral seesaw of śubha and aśubha set down. What remains when all that is renounced? The verse answers in one word, placed like a signature: bhaktimān — *full of love*. The emptying was never toward emptiness; everything else left so that devotion could have the whole house.
verses.connection: The portrait's secret revealed: every renunciation listed was making room for love.
verses.reflection: Make room for love today by quieting one of the four: exulting, hating, grieving, craving.
verses.background: The chapter closes with the portrait of the devotee dear to Krishna: hating none, friendly and compassionate, free of 'I' and 'mine', even in pleasure and pain, content, self-governed, agitating no one and unagitated, the same in honor and disgrace — and the seal: those who follow this immortal dharma with faith, holding Me supreme, are exceedingly dear to Me.
verses.hook: Who rises above joy and grief, craving and hatred?

refs.note: One who attains divine love neither craves nor grieves, neither hates nor delights in worldly things; this matches the devotee who neither rejoices nor laments.

views.text: Each verb has its object: no joy at gaining the coveted, no fretting at meeting the unwanted, no lament at losing the dear, no hankering for what is not yet had.
He gives up merit as well as demerit, because merit binds just as surely as demerit; there is no difference between them in this respect.
Devotees steeped in God's bliss rise above worldly pleasure and despair, give up both sinful and merely ritual action by offering everything to God, and are filled with a love that keeps growing.

verses.devanagari:
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः ।
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः॥
verses.transliteration:
samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ
śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅgavivarjitaḥ
verses.essence: Equal toward enemy and friend, and in honor and disgrace; equal in cold and heat, joy and sorrow; free of attachment —
verses.translation: He who is the same to foe and friend, and also in honor and dishonor, who is the same in cold and heat, in pleasure and pain, and who is free from attachment.

anvaya.parts: मान (honour) + अपमान (dishonour): honour and dishonour, joined by 'and'

anvaya.meaning: in cold and heat, joy and sorrow
anvaya.parts: शीत (cold) + उष्ण (heat) + सुख (joy) + दुःख (sorrow): a list of four, joined by 'and'
सङ्ग (attachment) + विवर्जित (freed from): one freed from attachment

verses.explanation: The equality ladder climbs its full height: weather (cold-heat), feeling (joy-sorrow), reputation (honor-disgrace), and at the top the steepest rung — śatrau ca mitre ca, enemy and friend met with the same face. For Arjuna, looking across a field at men who are precisely both, the phrase is not abstract ethics; it is his Tuesday.
verses.connection: The evenness of chapters 2–6 returns — now as a lover's trait rather than a technique.
verses.reflection: Try one hour of the steep equality: the same inner face toward a friend and toward a difficult one.
verses.background: The chapter closes with the portrait of the devotee dear to Krishna: hating none, friendly and compassionate, free of 'I' and 'mine', even in pleasure and pain, content, self-governed, agitating no one and unagitated, the same in honor and disgrace — and the seal: those who follow this immortal dharma with faith, holding Me supreme, are exceedingly dear to Me.
verses.text_note: The translation of this verse was missing in the source dataset; it is taken from the Sivananda text in the gita/gita dataset.
verses.hook: How does a true devotee stand before friend and foe, honor and insult?

views.text: Goes beyond the general non-hatred of 12.13: this is evenness kept up while foe and friend are actually standing before one, the mark of a more advanced devotee.
The devotee is equal to friend and foe, as Prahlāda judged his own son and his Guru's son without bias, and is unmoved by honor, dishonor, heat or cold because the mind is absorbed in God.

verses.devanagari:
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येन केनचित् ।
अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः॥
verses.transliteration:
tulyanindāstutirmaunī santuṣṭo yena kenacit
aniketaḥ sthiramatirbhaktimānme priyo naraḥ
verses.essence: — alike in blame and praise, silent, content with whatever comes, homeless, steady-minded, full of devotion: that one is dear to me.
verses.translation: He to whom censure and praise are equal, who is silent, content with anything, homeless, of a steady mind, and full of devotion that man is dear to Me.

anvaya.base: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुति · same in censure and praise
anvaya.parts: तुल्य (equal) + निन्दा (blame) + स्तुति (praise): one to whom blame and praise are equal
अ (without) + निकेत (dwelling): one without a fixed dwelling
स्थिर (steady) + मति (mind, thought): one whose mind is steady

anvaya.form: pronoun, genitive/dative singular, short form (to/for me)

verses.explanation: The portrait's last strokes: tulya-nindā-stutiḥ — the two voices that rule most lives, criticism and applause, finally at the same volume; maunī, the silence of one with nothing to defend; aniketaḥ, homeless — read literally by renunciants, inwardly by householders: at home everywhere because rooted nowhere circumstantial. And once more, bhaktimān: love, the trait the list cannot stop repeating.
verses.connection: Completes the seven-verse portrait — before 12.20 turns it into an invitation.
verses.reflection: Turn praise and blame to the same volume for one day — and find home wherever you are standing.
verses.background: The chapter closes with the portrait of the devotee dear to Krishna: hating none, friendly and compassionate, free of 'I' and 'mine', even in pleasure and pain, content, self-governed, agitating no one and unagitated, the same in honor and disgrace — and the seal: those who follow this immortal dharma with faith, holding Me supreme, are exceedingly dear to Me.
verses.hook: How does a true devotee respond to praise, blame and having little?

views.text: Content with whatever keeps the body going; homeless, with no fixed residence. Devotion is named again and again in this chapter because it is the means to knowledge.
Takes aniketa as one with no fixed resolve in worldly life, no 'this alone must be done by me'; such a person takes pleasure and pain as they come.
Love for God burns so brightly in the devotee that praise and blame, comfort and hardship lose their hold; like Ramakrishna facing illness, such a person does not pull the mind away from God.

verses.devanagari:
ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते ।
श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः॥
verses.transliteration:
ye tu dharmyāmṛtamidaṃ yathoktaṃ paryupāsate
śraddadhānā matparamā bhaktāste'tīva me priyāḥ
verses.essence: But those who honor this nectar of dharma as it has been declared, full of faith, holding me as supreme — those devotees are exceedingly dear to me.
verses.translation: They verily who follow this immortal Dharma (law or doctrine) as described above, endowed with faith, regarding Me as their supreme goal, they, the devotees, are exceedingly dear to Me.

anvaya.parts: धर्म्य (in accord with dharma) + अमृत (nectar of immortality): the nectar that is one with dharma
यथा (as) + उक्त (said): as it has been said

anvaya.base: परि + उप + √आस् · to worship all around, honour

anvaya.parts: मत् (me) + परम (highest): those for whom I am the highest

anvaya.form: pronoun, genitive/dative singular, short form (to/for me)

verses.explanation: The closing widens the door: the superlative — atīva me priyāḥ, *exceedingly* dear — goes not to those who have completed the portrait but to those who paryupāsate, who keep honoring it, walking toward it with faith. The standard of 12.13–19 might discourage; this verse insures against that: the attempt itself, sincerely sustained, already receives the fullest love. The chapter ends, fittingly, mid-embrace.
verses.connection: Seals the bhakti chapter: the portrait was the destination; faith-filled practice of it is already arrival.
verses.reflection: You need not finish the portrait to be loved — follow it with faith today, and be already exceedingly dear.
verses.background: The chapter closes with the portrait of the devotee dear to Krishna: hating none, friendly and compassionate, free of 'I' and 'mine', even in pleasure and pain, content, self-governed, agitating no one and unagitated, the same in honor and disgrace — and the seal: those who follow this immortal dharma with faith, holding Me supreme, are exceedingly dear to Me.
verses.hook: Who among devotees is dearest of all to God?

views.text: These are monks whose devotion is knowledge of the supreme Reality; the nectar is called so because, inseparable from virtue, it leads to immortality. The verse completes what 7.17 hinted.

The nectar is the bhakti-yoga of 12.2: at once virtuous duty and nectar, since even as a means it gives the bliss of the goal. The chapter thus closes on devotion's superiority over self-contemplation.
Dharma itself is nectar because it is the means to immortality; he notes that some read the compound as dharmyāmṛtam.
Closing the chapter, Krishna sums up his answer: devotion to his personal form is the highest path, and those who make him their goal and live these virtues with faith are exceedingly dear to him.
